newsitem.title: CHINA: ATHLETICS-CHINA'S WANG JUNXIA NOT TO COMPETE IN 97.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-CHINA'S WANG JUNXIA NOT TO COMPETE IN 97.

text.p: Chinese Olympic running champion Wang Junxia will not run in any competitions this year to recover from a series of illness and injuries, the Yangcheng Evening News said in an edition available in Beijing on Sunday.
Wang Junxia had been continually hampered by sickness and injury after the Atlanta Olympics, where she won gold in the 5,000 metres, the June 28 edition of the newspaper said.
"This year, will be a year of adjustment, and she will not be participating in any competitions," said the newspaper, which is based in the southern province of Guangzhou.

The star runner, who shot to international fame in 1993 when she shattered the world records for the 3,000 and 10,000 metres, also would not run in China's Eighth National Games to be held in October, it said.
Wang was now studying law at northeastern Liaoning University in her home province of Liaoning, and was swimming and playing ball games to recuperate, it said.

The newspaper did not elaborate on her injuries, but earlier reports have said Wang was forced to stop her rigorous training regimen after contracting neurasthenia, a nervous disorder that causes fatigue and anxiety.
Wang still hoped to run in the 2000 Olympics in Sydney, the newspaper said.
"If my physical condition allows, I will still give it my best," it quoted her as saying.
